original_test_intent: Complete exactly 100 approved DC cycles covering main and standby power behavior and prove reliable OS boot plus stable PCIe, MCTP and the engineering-resolved SSIF/SMA/FPGA set on every cycle.
original_method: Pin the Vera Rubin guide and authoritative dual-domain DC sequence, drain workloads for the 24-hour window, run a durable 100-cycle state machine with external rail/console observation, collect full endpoint and error evidence, and halt on the first anomaly.
manual_activity: An operator approves and monitors the 100-cycle dual-domain run, confirms main/standby transitions through independent evidence, reviews every failure boundary and keeps the recovery path external to the affected BMC domain.

Main/standby power-domain topology and authoritative DC sequence
External control/restore method if BMC loses standby power
Decision whether required health covers SSIF, SMA, FPGA or all three

Secure secrets and sufficient immutable artifact storage
safety_requirements: Do not report five cycles as completion of the explicit 100
Do not assume chassis off removes standby or that the BMC can restore itself after standby loss
Never expose passwords or disable host verification
Persist cycle and rail state atomically; never silently skip or double-count
Stop and preserve first incomplete rail transition, restore-control loss, boot timeout, endpoint mismatch, AER/DPC, storage/data, thermal/power or recovery failure
No automatic retry or evidence overwrite
agent_execution_scope: Verify guide, domain topology, resolved endpoint matrix and runner readiness
Collect comprehensive read-only baseline and approved preflight only

Compare OS/PCIe/MCTP/resolved endpoint and error/health evidence
Perform no guessed standby control, shortcut, retry, failure suppression, workload restore or verdict

Approve 100-cycle timing, outage/data state, limits and external recovery

command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use a secure durable 100-cycle runner implementing the approved main-plus-standby state machine with external observation and complete per-cycle endpoint/error collection.

modernized_recommendation.status: CRITICAL 100-CYCLE DUAL-DOMAIN DC QUALIFICATION PENDING GUIDE AND HEALTH-MATRIX DECISIONS
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Represent main/standby transitions and each cycle as immutable state records; advance only after external rail proof and complete OS/PCIe/MCTP/resolved endpoint evidence, halting on the first anomaly.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds the missing standby mechanism, guide/criteria decisions, secure durable accounting and complete evidence while rejecting the five-cycle generic loop.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Five generic host power cycles cannot establish 100-cycle endurance or standby/BMC cold initialization. AER/PCIe counts cannot substitute for MCTP, SSIF, SMA or FPGA stability.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Removing standby may kill the control plane that drives restoration, and repeated cycles can reveal intermittent failures that a retry hides. External restore capability and first-failure preservation are mandatory.

project_override_considerations: A five-cycle preflight may validate the runner only. Any unsupported health field or rail operation needs exact guide authority and remains outside the pass denominator; AC or warm-stress evidence is not interchangeable.

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure requires 100 main-plus-standby cycles and SSIF/SMA stability, while Criteria names FPGA instead; DeepSeek reduces coverage to five generic host power cycles with no standby proof or named-interface checks. These are material coverage conflicts.

review_improvement: Restores 100-cycle dual-domain coverage, exposes the SSIF/SMA/FPGA mismatch and requires external recovery plus complete per-cycle endpoint evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: DC-2 endurance measures both repeated host-power recovery and cold initialization of standby-powered management domains. A generic chassis command may never cross that boundary, while loss of standby can remove the issuer itself. Atomic external rail proof and endpoint manifests are therefore necessary; otherwise successful OS boots could hide untested standby paths, missing management endpoints or retried intermittent failures.
